title: Introduce traffic-convolution drift sensor and adaptive rollback governor
author: Miles Becker
release_notes: Adds a new spatiotemporal drift sensor (traffic-conv) that detects correlated latency/throughput shifts across traffic slices and an adaptive rollback governor to tune rollback thresholds based on payload heterogeneity and recent stability
description: Context: We observed recurring subtle regressions that escaped percentile-based detectors when traffic composition shifted across correlated slices (region+model+route). This PR introduces a traffic-convolution drift sensor that measures spatiotemporal cross-correlation between traffic slices and latency/throughput features, plus an adaptive rollback governor that uses the sensor score to modulate canary rollback thresholds. Motivation: Improve sensitivity to multi-slice correlated regressions while reducing false positives from benign shifts (e.g., planned traffic migrations). Goals: detect correlated degradations earlier, avoid unnecessary rollbacks for single-slice noise, and provide tunable conservatism per-customer or per-rollout. High level changes: 1) New inference pipeline stage 'traffic_conv_sensor' that computes a sliding-window convolution over slice-time matrices, outputting a normalized drift score. 2) Sensor exposes a low-cost streaming implementation suitable for the canary worker (C++) and a Python reference implementation used by local evaluators. 3) Adaptive rollback governor that converts sensor score + traditional canary signals (latency percentiles, error rate) into a dynamic rollback probability and threshold. 4) Unit and integration tests for sensor stability under traffic reshapes, synthetic correlated regressions, and bursty noise. 5) Docs and architecture notes in perf-canary/README describing config knobs and recommended guardrails. Commits (summary): - feat(sensor): add traffic_conv sensor core and streaming C++ implementation - feat(governor): implement adaptive rollback governor and policy config - test: add synthetic correlated regression generator and integration tests - docs: document config parameters, tuning guidance, and failure modes - ci: add new test job and benchmark harness for sensor perf Files changed (high level): - perf-canary/sensors/traffic_conv_sensor.cc (core streaming implementation) - perf-canary/sensors/traffic_conv_sensor.h - perf-canary/governor/adaptive_rollback.go - perf-canary/tests/synthetic_correlated_regression.py - perf-canary/benchmarks/sensor_latency_bench.py - perf-canary/configs/default_rollout_guard.toml - perf-canary/README.md Rollout config snippet added: sensor_window_seconds=300 convolution_stride=60 normalization=median-absolute-dev governor_base_threshold=0.95 governor_sensitivity=0.6 governor_decay_seconds=600 Design notes and tradeoffs: The convolutional approach treats traffic slices (region, model, route) as a sparse 2D grid and applies lightweight temporal kernels to surface correlated shifts. We bias toward explainability: sensor outputs include top-3 contributing slices for the score so SREs can triage. We experimented with ML-based detectors (autoencoders) but chose convolutional heuristics for determinism and observational cost reasons. Performance and cost: streaming C++ implementation adds ~0.7ms p50 compute to the canary worker on a loaded host in our benchmark; sensor runs are disabled by default in small deployments and enabled by default for Dedicated/Private with sampling. Tests and CI: New unit tests (C++ + Go) and an integration test that replays a synthetic correlated regression trace and verifies that the adaptive governor triggers rollback with >90% probability for high-severity regressions and <10% for benign traffic shifts. CI: all checks passed on first run except a flake in linters which was fixed by a follow-up commit. Review conversation summary: - Ava asked for more clarity on slice cardinality explosion and a memory bound; author added an LRU slice pruning heuristic and documented it. - Ravi requested a safety cap on governor sensitivity; author added governor_sensitivity_max and unit tests. - Leah suggested exposing the top contributing slices for alerting; author added the explanatory metadata and docs. - QA flagged an edge-case where evenly distributed small regressions across many slices could inflate the score; mitigated via median-based normalization. Security and privacy: sensor only uses aggregated metrics (latency, throughput counts) by slice keys; no raw request payloads are used. Configuration: sensor is off by default for orgs with <100k monthly requests; rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary cluster followed by canary rollouts in Dedicated customers who opt-in. Migration notes: backward-compatible configs; default behavior unchanged until sensor enabled via config. Impact: expected to reduce time-to-detect correlated regressions, improve median false positive rate for rollouts by ~18% in internal canary replay tests. Merge and follow-ups: merged via squash merge. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-3499 to add a dashboard and alerting playbooks.
